reason: Correct source locator: DPWH Official PD 1096 RIRR p.230 lists Section 1603 as Glazing of Openings; p.232 lists Section 1608 as Exterior Veneer.

proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XVI, Sec. 1608, plastic veneer on exterior walls is limited to the first storey as the standard rule. What is the exception, and what maximum height does it allow?

options.text: Exception for buildings outside highly restrictive zones: plastic veneer may extend up to 10.00 m above grade
Exception for fire-sprinklered buildings: plastic veneer may extend to the full building height, provided the building does not exceed 20 storeys
Exception for Type V buildings: plastic veneer may extend up to 15.00 m above grade, if the building is located in a non-seismic zone
Exception for approved plastic types: veneer is permitted on all storeys regardless of height, as long as it passes fire safety tests

proposed.rationale: Sec. 1608 standard rule limits exterior plastic veneer to the first storey. The exception — applicable outside highly restrictive fire zones — permits plastic veneer to extend up to 10.00 m above grade. This exception is zone-dependent, not sprinkler-dependent, and the 10.00 m limit is a hard ceiling even in less restrictive zones.
proposed.explanation: The standard (1st storey) versus exception (10.00 m outside highly restrictive zones) pairing is the primary testable fact of Sec. 1608. The zone-dependency of the exception — not sprinklers — is the key discriminator.
